I am an old woman here in Machinga, farming this small maize plot by myself. My plot is very small, only a little piece, and I have no money to waste. Last year I got a coupon from the government for one bag of fertilizer and some seed — I am waiting to see if I get one again this year, because without that coupon I cannot buy fertilizer from the shop, it is too expensive for me. I always put the maize together with pigeon pea and pumpkin so my family has something to eat even if one crop fails. I do my own work on this plot with my hands and my hoe; I cannot pay anyone to help me.

For the fertilizer, if the coupon comes, I will put that one bag of NPK at planting and the urea for top-dressing like the extension man showed the village last time. On my small piece, one bag of each is what fits. If no coupon comes, I will just plant and hope for rain, and put the little ash and goat droppings I gather from around the house. I keep some seed from last year's harvest because it grew well, but if I get the subsidy seed I will plant that one because it gives more cobs. I do not buy chemicals for spraying — I just pull the weeds myself. There is no river near my plot, so I wait for the rains. My children and grandchildren help me sometimes at planting and at harvest, but most days it is just me with my hoe.
